subject.title: Plugin `message_sending` hooks silently bypassed on channel agent-reply delivery paths (2026.5.26, still present in 2026.6.1)

question: Which hook ownership model should become canonical for the `message_sending` agent-reply bypass: the broad exactly-once Telegram streaming repair, a dispatcher-only repair, or a maintainer-owned replacement?
rationale: The bug is real, but the remaining choice changes where a documented safety hook is enforced and whether Telegram delivery owns an opt-out to avoid duplicate invocation.

options.title: Select The Broad Exactly-Once Repair
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216 or an equivalent maintainer repair as the canonical path after rebase, suffix repair, and proof refresh.

options.title: Land Dispatcher-Only First
options.body: Take a narrower branch such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92976 for configured `beforeDeliver` and keep Telegram streamed-final coverage tracked separately.

options.title: Replace With Maintainer-Owned Patch
options.body: Close or pause the overlapping branches and build a smaller maintainer-owned fix that explicitly defines hook ownership across dispatcher and Telegram delivery.

recommendation.title: Select The Broad Exactly-Once Repair
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216 or an equivalent maintainer repair as the canonical path after rebase, suffix repair, and proof refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent hook-correlation and Telegram delivery history make this the best available owner for the hook boundary choice.
